library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

df <- read_csv("data/Snow_Emergency_Victory2_Tows_2023.csv")

# Basic summaries
dim(df)          # rows, columns
glimpse(df)      # variable types
summary(df)      # quick stats

# Missingness by column
df %>% summarise(across(everything(),
                        ~ mean(is.na(.)),
                        .names = "prop_na_{.col}"))

# Simple visualizations
df %>%
  count(Ward, sort = TRUE) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Ward, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Tows by Ward", x = "Ward", y = "Count")

df %>%
  count(Neighborho, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Neighborho, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Neighborhoods by Tows",
       x = "Neighborhood", y = "Count")


# Question 5

# Install once (if you haven't already):
# install.packages("sf")

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# If you already read the data earlier, reuse that object
# e.g. df <- readr::read_csv("data/Snow_Emergency_Victory2_Tows_2023.csv")

# Check column names so you know what the coordinate columns are
names(df)

# Replace "Longitude" and "Latitude" below with your actual column names
tows_sf <- st_as_sf(
  df,
  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),  # e.g. c("X", "Y") or c("LONGITUDE", "LATITUDE")
  crs = 4326,                           # WGS84 lat/long
  remove = FALSE
)

# Basic point map of all tows
ggplot(tows_sf) +
  geom_sf(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Snow Emergency Tow Locations",
    subtitle = "Victory2, 2023",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# We told it to add Minneapolis and roads

# Install once if needed:
# install.packages("sf")
# install.packages("tigris")

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tigris)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# --- 1. Make sure your tow points exist as sf ----
# (You should already have something like this; adjust col names if needed.)
# df <- readr::read_csv("data/Snow_Emergency_Victory2_Tows_2023.csv")
# tows_sf <- st_as_sf(df, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# --- 2. Get Minneapolis city boundary (from Census via tigris) ----
mpls <- places("MN", cb = TRUE, year = 2020) |>
  filter(NAME == "Minneapolis") |>
  st_transform(26915)   # project to a local UTM-ish CRS

# Transform tow points to same CRS
tows_sf_utm <- st_transform(tows_sf, st_crs(mpls))

# --- 3. Get road lines (Hennepin County) ----
# 053 = Hennepin County FIPS code
roads_henn <- roads("MN", "053", year = 2020) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(mpls))

# Optional: keep only roads that intersect Minneapolis boundary
roads_mpls <- st_intersection(roads_henn, mpls)

# --- 4. Plot: boundary + roads + tow points ----
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = mpls, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = roads_mpls, color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = tows_sf_utm, color = "red", alpha = 0.6, size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Snow Emergency Tow Locations in Minneapolis",
    subtitle = "Victory2, 2023",
    x = "Easting", y = "Northing"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
